sections.title: Income and spending
sections.content:
Precise vocabulary for discussing financial situations:
• affluent — having a great deal of money; wealthy. They live in an affluent neighbourhood.
• frugal — careful with money; not wasteful. My grandmother was always frugal, saving every penny.
• extravagant — spending excessively. The wedding was incredibly extravagant.
• revenue — income, especially of a company. The company's annual revenue exceeded expectations.
• disposable income — money available after essential costs. Rising rent leaves people with less disposable income.

sections.title: Debt and financial trouble
sections.content:
Words for describing financial difficulties:
• bankrupt — legally declared unable to pay debts. The business went bankrupt after two years.
• mortgage — a loan to buy property. They took out a 25-year mortgage on the house.
• debt — money owed to others. Student debt has become a serious issue worldwide.
• inflation — the rate at which prices rise. High inflation reduces the purchasing power of wages.
• recession — a period of economic decline. The 2008 recession affected millions of families.

sections.title: Investments and savings
sections.content:
Financial planning vocabulary:
• dividend — a share of company profits paid to shareholders. The company announced a generous dividend this quarter.
• portfolio — a range of investments held by a person. She diversified her investment portfolio wisely.
• asset — something of value owned by a person or company. Property is often considered a safe asset.
• lucrative — producing a great deal of profit. The tech industry can be extremely lucrative.

exercises.question: A person who is very careful with money and avoids waste is:
exercises.explanation: Frugal means sparing or economical with regard to money or resources.

exercises.question: When prices across the economy rise over time, this is called:
exercises.hint: Your money buys less than before.
exercises.explanation: Inflation is a general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money.

exercises.question: Something that generates a large amount of profit is:
exercises.explanation: Lucrative means producing a great deal of profit.

exercises.question: A long-term loan used to purchase a house is a:
exercises.explanation: A mortgage is a legal agreement to borrow money from a bank to buy a home.

exercises.question: The total income generated by a business is its:
exercises.explanation: Revenue is the income that a business generates from its normal operations.

exercises.question: A wealthy area where rich people live is described as:
exercises.explanation: Affluent means having a great deal of money; wealthy.

exercises.question: A period of significant economic decline is a:
exercises.hint: The economy shrinks during this time.
exercises.explanation: A recession is a period of temporary economic decline identified by a fall in GDP.

exercises.question: A range of investments held by an individual is their:
exercises.hint: It contains stocks, bonds, property, etc.
exercises.explanation: A portfolio is a range of investments held by a person or organization.
